correctness.rationale: Tree T(k,s) has |V|=s+4k+1, |E|=|V|-1 and diameter six for k>=2. Invariant rigid white anchor branches ensure independent floating fair coins while the hub is blue. For s=k-1, U survives each step with probability 1-2^-k and exits geometrically; three rounds of white floating vertices force the all-white absorbing state with probability at least 2^-3k, yielding the finite expectation bound and making E tau_abs>=2^k. For s=k+1, hub has k+1 fixed blue neighbors versus at most k white and the 2^k floating patterns form a complete, closed, uniform transition class. Exact rational code tested k=2..7.

value.rationale: The source leaves open whether exponentially slow and exponentially rich stochastic majority behavior requires cyclic interaction structure. The two diameter-six tree families establish that acyclicity and low radius do not prevent either phenomenon. Exact geometric waiting and one-step-uniform recurrent class distinguish the mechanism and give quantitatively interpretable complexity, not just an arbitrary sampled counterexample.
